children.desc: Ligusticum canadense, known by the common names of American lovage, boar hog root, and Canadian licorice-root, is a member of the carrot family, Apiaceae.

children.name: Ligusticum grayi
children.desc: Ligusticum grayi is a species of flowering plant in the carrot family known by the common name Gray's licorice-root.

children.name: Ligusticum porteri
children.desc: Ligusticum porteri, also known as osha or Porter lovage, is a perennial herb found in parts of the Rocky Mountains and northern New Mexico, in the southwestern United States.

children.name: Ligusticum scothicum
children.desc: Ligusticum scoticum, known as Scots lovage, or Scottish licorice-root, is a perennial flowering plant in the celery family, Apiaceae.

desc: Apiaceae, also called Umbelliferae, is a family of mostly aromatic flowering plants named after the type genus Apium, and commonly known as the celery, carrot, or parsley family, or as umbellifers.
